Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

lagprotest (development version)

  • lagged_protest() now returns continuous measures of evidence and strength computed from the same permutations as the p-values: per-lag z and a in the profile, and in effect the lag of the largest z, its standardized position Z among the permuted maxima, and the chance-corrected A and RV coefficient. The permuted RV values are kept in null.rv. print() and summary() show them, and lagged_protest_pairs() adds Z and A as columns.

  • lagged_protest() now reports the mean lag-1 autocorrelation of each series (ar1), raw and after removing the seasonal harmonics, as a description of how close the data are to the conditions under which the phase scheme was liberal in simulations.

  • lagged_protest() now issues a message when the smallest attainable p-value is 0.05 or more (e.g., the cyclic scheme without mirror at n = 12).

  • The documentation of lagged_protest() and the permutation-schemes article cite Manly and Navarro Alberto (2020) for the p-value formula and the recommended number of permutations, and pp. 83–84 for the max-statistic adjustment of correlated tests.

  • The liver example article now checks the lag scan with two statistics that weigh all lags equally (minP and the standardized m²), computed from the surrogates stored in each fit. The raw minimum m² favors long lags, and the climate–histochemistry delay is weaker under the balanced statistics.

  • The permutation loop is about five times faster: m² and the RV coefficient of each permuted pair are now computed directly from the singular values of the cross-product matrix instead of calling vegan::procrustes() for every permutation. Results with a fixed seed are unchanged (p-values and lags identical, m² equal to floating-point rounding); a new regression test guards them.

  • lagged_protest() and simulate_lagged_series() now check their arguments and name the offending one in the error: nperm and seed must be single whole numbers, lags must not be empty, mirror, bidirectional and scale must be TRUE or FALSE, and the counts, period, amplitude and noise_sd of the simulator must be valid. Previously, nperm = 2.5 was silently truncated and an invalid seed produced an unrelated warning.

  • The minimum-P message no longer suggests mirror = TRUE when the cyclic scheme already uses it.

  • The fits stored by lagged_protest_pairs() now carry a call that names the data sets and shows the values of lags, bidirectional and seed, so print() is informative and eval(fit$call) reproduces the fit.

  • lagged_protest_pairs() gains the columns effect_lag (the lag to which Z and A refer, which can differ from optimal_lag) and RV.

  • summary() now returns an object of class "summary.lagged_protest" (still a data frame) whose print() method shows the global p-value, the effect measures and the autocorrelation below the profile; before, these were attributes that were not printed.

  • print() notes when the optimal lag (smallest m²) and the effect lag (largest z) differ, and no longer runs the lines of a long call together.

  • The documentation of lagged_protest(), the “Get started” vignette and the README now explain that the smallest m² favors the longest lags scanned, describe the effect measures and ar1, and point to lagged_protest_pairs(), autoplot() and the liver example. Smaller fixes: the mirror element is documented, n_perm is described as the same at every lag, and the per-lag adjustment that lagged_protest_pairs() cannot set is noted.

  • New inst/CITATION, so citation("lagprotest") gives the Zenodo DOI.

lagprotest 0.6.0

  • New as.data.frame() method returns the lag profile in long form, with the permutation null quantile at each lag and a flag for the optimal lag.
  • New autoplot() method draws the lag profile with ggplot2 (suggested package), marking the optimal lag and its global p-value as plot() does.

lagprotest 0.5.0

  • New data set dminutus_liver: monthly means of four hepatic modules and of climate for the treefrog Dendropsophus minutus over one annual cycle (Franco-Belussi et al. 2026, CC BY 4.0), with a new article analyzing it with lagged_protest_pairs().

lagprotest 0.4.0

  • New lagged_protest_pairs() runs lagged_protest() on pairs of data sets from a named list (by default all unordered pairs, both directions through the sign of the lag) and returns one table, with the global p-values adjusted across pairs ("BH" by default) and the fits kept in an attribute.
  • plot() now circles the optimal lag, filled when the global p-value is below alpha, and prints the global p-value above the plot (global = FALSE restores the previous plot).
  • Simulations of the period argument with the full design (1000 replicates per scenario, 12–96 time points) are summarized in the article “Choosing a permutation scheme”: after truncation the global p-value was calibrated up to AR(1) of 0.5 and liberal with strong autocorrelation, as for series spanning complete cycles.

lagprotest 0.3.0

  • New period argument in lagged_protest(): when the seasonal cycle does not divide the series length, both series are truncated to their first floor(n / period) * period rows, so that the phase and cyclic schemes, which treat the series as periodic with period n, remain calibrated. In simulations (24–48 time points, cycle of 0.75 n), this brought the Type I error of the global p-value from 0.46–0.94 back to 0.04–0.05 for AR(1) noise of 0.3. Removing the seasonal component by harmonic regression was also tested and left the test liberal, so it was not added.

lagprotest 0.2.0

Breaking changes

  • The default permutation scheme is now permutation = "phase" (phase-randomized surrogates), which retains power for the global p-value across lags. Use permutation = "cyclic" for the previous behavior; the phase scheme is random, so set seed for reproducible results.

  • lagged_protest() now defaults to p.adjust.method = "none", because corrections such as Holm are often unattainable with the few permutations of the cyclic scheme. $p.value is now the raw p-value at the optimal lag; the adjusted value is in the new $p.adjusted element, and the number of permutations in $n_perm. print() warns when p-values are unadjusted.

New features

  • lagged_protest() returns a global p-value, $p.global, for the scan across lags. It is a max-statistic test that compares the observed minimum m² across lags with the minimum across lags under each permutation, and so accounts for testing several lags and selecting the optimal one. print() reports it below the optimal lag. Simulations showed that the raw p-value at the optimal lag rejects 10–28% of the time (21–25% on average) when the series are independent.
  • New scheme permutation = "phase": phase-randomized surrogates of Y that keep the amplitude spectrum of each column and the cross-spectra among columns. Unlike cyclic shifts, surrogates do not reproduce the observed alignment at other lags, so the global p-value keeps its power.
  • p.adjust.method = "maxT" gives single-step max-statistic adjusted p-values per lag.
  • permutation = "free" now applies each permutation jointly to all lags, as the max-statistic requires.

Infrastructure

  • Continuous integration: R CMD check on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu, and test coverage reporting, via GitHub Actions.
  • Spell check of the documentation, contributing guide, code of conduct and issue templates.
  • The vignette now uses US English spelling.

lagprotest 0.1.0

First public release.

  • lagged_protest() scans Procrustes concordance between two ordered multivariate series across candidate lags and tests each lag by permutation. Two schemes are available: cyclic shifts of the full series, optionally with time reversal (default), and free row permutation as in vegan::protest(). P-values are adjusted across lags. Accepts matrices, data frames or dist objects (converted by PCoA).
  • print(), summary(), plot() and residuals() methods for the lag profile, the optimal lag and per-observation Procrustes residuals.
  • simulate_lagged_series() generates seasonal series with AR(1) noise and a known lag, for calibration and power studies.
